rationale:
Evidence from iteration 6 (score 790.9, best so far): oval finishes 20 of 20 (progress 0.998), s-bend finishes 20 of 20 (progress 0.997), and slalom finishes 6 of 20 (progress 0.76, 14 off-track ends, 0.75 line-loss events, max_error 0.055). Moving the sensors forward from y=0.04 to y=0.06 gave the largest gain of any change so far: slalom progress rose from 0.53 to 0.76 and the slalom finish rate from 0.05 to 0.30. Steering oscillation stayed at 0.24 to 0.37, well below the 0.5 warning level, so damping is not the limit. Slalom control_effort rose to 15.2, which suggests the robot is still correcting hard on alternating bends. The sensor lead is therefore the lever that is working. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06), and edge coverage was shown to be a small effect in iteration 5.

Change: move all five sensors forward again, from y=0.06 to y=0.07 m (within the 0.08 limit), keeping the same x spread (-0.04 to +0.04 m), sensor size 0.016 and spacing. This extends the phase lead on alternating bends so the correction starts earlier. Everything else is held at iteration 6 values (kp 5.0, kd 1.4, ki 0.01, base_speed 1.2, mass 0.6, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, sensor weights, line_loss last_direction), so the change can be read cleanly against iteration 6.

Expected result: slalom progress above 0.85 and slalom finishes rising to about 10 of 20 or more, with oval and s-bend completion holding near 1.0. Hypotheses: (a) if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.5 on any track, the lead is overcorrecting and kd should go up to about 1.6 or kp down to about 4.6. (b) If slalom progress is flat versus iteration 6, lag is no longer the limit and the next step is more steering authority, either kp about 5.5 with kd 1.5 or a narrower wheel_track of about 0.11 m to raise turn rate per unit turn. (c) If oval or s-bend completion drops, the sensors are now too far ahead on the sharp bends and y should return to 0.06. Next measurements: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort per track, so the lead effect can be separated from the gain effects.
